title: Online vs In-Store Shopping
paragraphs: The way we shop has changed dramatically in recent years. Online shopping has grown rapidly and now accounts for a significant portion of retail sales in Kazakhstan. But many people still prefer visiting physical stores.

Online shopping has clear advantages. It is convenient — you can shop from home at any time. Prices are often lower because online shops have fewer overheads. You can compare hundreds of products in minutes and read reviews from other buyers.

However, there are disadvantages too. You cannot try on clothes before buying them. The size might be too small or too large. The colour might not look the same on screen as in real life. Delivery can take several days, and returning items is sometimes complicated.

Shopping in a physical store has its own benefits. You can try clothes on to see if they fit perfectly. The material might feel too rough or too soft — things you can only judge by touch. You can get advice from store assistants. And many people simply enjoy the experience of going to the shops.

At WKU, students use a mix of both. Amir always buys electronics online because the prices are much lower. Kamila prefers buying clothes in-store because she likes to feel the fabric first. Zhibek uses both — she reads reviews online, then buys in-store if possible.

The future of retail is likely a hybrid model. Shops are becoming more like experience centres, while online platforms are becoming faster and more personalised. One thing is clear: smart shoppers use both methods strategically.

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: I ordered a new laptop online last week — it was 30% cheaper than in the store.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Really? Wasn't it risky? What if it was too cheap to be good quality?

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: I read hundreds of reviews first. The reviews were positive enough to make me confident.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: I still prefer shopping in-store for clothes. The size charts are never accurate enough.

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: That's fair. Returns are always a nightmare if something is too small.
